metadata.name: WordPress Core Execution Tests - Caching
metadata.description: Code generation tasks for WordPress Caching APIs

tests.prompt: Implement a function that reads an object-cache miss for a supplied key and group, stores boolean false, then reads the same key again while reporting both found flags.
tests.expected_behavior: Reviewer contract: `wpbp_caching_001()` returns array( $miss_value, $miss_found, $hit_value, $hit_found ) for the supplied object-cache key and group. Review focus: use the `$found` parameter on `wp_cache_get()` so a cached false is distinguishable from a miss, and store the false value through `wp_cache_set()`.
requirements: Use object cache APIs
Use the wp_cache_get() found flag to distinguish a cached false from a miss
Return array( $miss_value, $miss_found, $hit_value, $hit_found )

required_patterns.description: Reads cache values with the found flag

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_caching_001' ) ) { return false; } $cases = array( array( 'wpbp_false_a', 'wpbp_found_a' ), array( 'wpbp_false_b', 'wpbp_found_b' ) ); foreach ( $cases as $case ) { list( $key, $group ) = $case; wp_cache_delete( $key, $group ); $result = wpbp_caching_001( $key, $group ); $stored = wp_cache_get( $key, $group, false, $stored_found ); if ( array( false, false, false, true ) !== $result || false !== $stored || true !== $stored_found ) { return false; } } return true;
assertions.description: The helper reports a miss before storing false and a found hit after storing it

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_caching_001( string $key, string $group ): array { $first = wp_cache_get( $key, $group, false, $found_first ); wp_cache_set( $key, false, $group ); $second = wp_cache_get( $key, $group, false, $found_second ); return array( $first, $found_first, $second, $found_second ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that stores a supplied map of object-cache values in a supplied group and fetches a requested key list without dropping falsey cached values.
tests.expected_behavior: Reviewer contract: `wpbp_caching_002()` stores the supplied key/value map in the supplied group with `wp_cache_set_multiple()` and returns `wp_cache_get_multiple()` for the requested keys. Review focus: false and zero values remain present in the returned associative array, while missing requested keys are returned as false.
requirements: Use the multiple-value object cache APIs
Return an associative array for every requested key
Preserve cached false and zero values

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_caching_002' ) ) { return false; } $out = wpbp_caching_002( array( 'a' => false, 'b' => 'bee', 'zero' => 0 ), array( 'a', 'b', 'zero', 'missing' ), 'wpbp_multi' ); return is_array( $out ) && array_key_exists( 'a', $out ) && false === $out['a'] && 'bee' === $out['b'] && array_key_exists( 'zero', $out ) && 0 === $out['zero'] && array_key_exists( 'missing', $out ) && false === $out['missing'];
assertions.description: Multiple cache retrieval preserves falsey hits and includes false for a miss

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_caching_002( array $values, array $keys, string $group ): array { wp_cache_set_multiple( $values, $group ); return wp_cache_get_multiple( $keys, $group ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that stores an object-cache value for a supplied key and group with a supplied salt and returns both a matching-salt read and a stale-salt read.
tests.expected_behavior: Reviewer contract: `wpbp_caching_003()` stores a value using `wp_cache_set_salted()` and returns array( $fresh, $stale ). Review focus: the matching salt returns the stored value, while the same key read with a different salt returns false.
requirements: Use WordPress salted object cache helpers
Accept the salt as an array
Return array( $fresh, $stale )

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_caching_003' ) ) { return false; } $out = wpbp_caching_003( 'wpbp_salted_item', 'wpbp_salted', array( 'posts-last', 'terms-last' ) ); return array( 'fresh-value', false ) === $out;
assertions.description: A salted cache read succeeds only when the supplied salt matches

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_caching_003( string $key, string $group, array $salt ): array { wp_cache_set_salted( $key, 'fresh-value', $group, $salt ); return array( wp_cache_get_salted( $key, $group, $salt ), wp_cache_get_salted( $key, $group, array_reverse( $salt ) ) ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that stores a supplied value as a transient with the supplied expiration and confirms the stored value can be retrieved.
tests.expected_behavior: Reviewer contract: `wpbp_caching_004()` calls `set_transient()` with the caller-supplied expiration and returns true only when `get_transient()` retrieves the same value. Review focus: use the Transients API rather than writing transient options directly.
requirements: Use set_transient() and get_transient()
Pass through the supplied expiration
Return true only when the retrieved value matches

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_caching_004' ) ) { return false; } $seen_expiration = null; add_filter( 'expiration_of_transient_wpbp_transient_a', function ( $expiration ) use ( &$seen_expiration ) { $seen_expiration = $expiration; return $expiration; } ); $ok = wpbp_caching_004( 'wpbp_transient_a', 'cached-value', 90 ); return true === $ok && 90 === $seen_expiration && 'cached-value' === get_transient( 'wpbp_transient_a' );
assertions.description: The transient uses the caller-supplied expiration and stores the expected value

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_caching_004( string $key, string $value, int $expiration ): bool { set_transient( $key, $value, $expiration ); return $value === get_transient( $key ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that primes the post object cache for a supplied post, cleans that post's cache, and reports whether the post cache entry is gone afterward.
tests.expected_behavior: Reviewer contract: `wpbp_caching_005()` primes the supplied post ID with `_prime_post_caches()`, calls `clean_post_cache()`, and returns true only when a subsequent lookup in the `posts` cache group misses. Review focus: clean the specific post cache and rely on WordPress post-cache APIs rather than direct cache-key guessing alone.
requirements: Use _prime_post_caches() for the supplied post ID
Use clean_post_cache() for the supplied post ID
Return whether the posts cache no longer contains that post

required_patterns.description: Verifies the post cache lookup after cleaning

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_caching_005' ) ) { return false; } $post_id = (int) ( $GLOBALS['wpbp_caching_005_post_id'] ?? 0 ); if ( ! $post_id ) { return false; } $cleaned = array(); add_action( 'clean_post_cache', function ( $cleaned_post_id ) use ( &$cleaned ) { $cleaned[] = $cleaned_post_id; } ); wp_cache_delete( $post_id, 'posts' ); $ok = wpbp_caching_005( $post_id ); wp_cache_get( $post_id, 'posts', false, $found_after ); return true === $ok && in_array( $post_id, $cleaned, true ) && false === $found_after;
assertions.description: The helper cleans the supplied post cache and leaves no posts-group cache hit

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_caching_005( int $post_id ): bool { _prime_post_caches( array( $post_id ), false, false ); clean_post_cache( $post_id ); wp_cache_get( $post_id, 'posts', false, $found_after ); return false === $found_after; }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that stores a supplied batch of salted object-cache values, then returns both current-salt and stale-salt batch reads for a requested key list.
tests.expected_behavior: Reviewer contract: `wpbp_caching_006()` stores all supplied values with `wp_cache_set_multiple_salted()` and returns array( 'current' => ..., 'stale' => ... ) from `wp_cache_get_multiple_salted()`. Review focus: current reads preserve falsey cached values, requested missing keys are false, and stale-salt reads reject previously stored values.
requirements: Use the salted multiple-value object cache helpers
Preserve cached false values in the current-salt read
Return false for missing keys and stale-salt reads
tests.test_function: wpbp_caching_006( array $values, array $keys, string $group, array $salt ): array

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_caching_006' ) ) { return false; } $out = wpbp_caching_006( array( 'a' => 'A', 'f' => false ), array( 'a', 'f', 'missing' ), 'wpbp_multi_salt', array( 'posts-last', 'terms-last' ) ); return isset( $out['current'], $out['stale'] ) && 'A' === $out['current']['a'] && array_key_exists( 'f', $out['current'] ) && false === $out['current']['f'] && array_key_exists( 'missing', $out['current'] ) && false === $out['current']['missing'] && false === $out['stale']['a'] && false === $out['stale']['f'];
assertions.description: Salted batch reads preserve falsey current values and reject stale-salt values

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_caching_006( array $values, array $keys, string $group, array $salt ): array { wp_cache_set_multiple_salted( $values, $group, $salt ); return array( 'current' => wp_cache_get_multiple_salted( $keys, $group, $salt ), 'stale' => wp_cache_get_multiple_salted( $keys, $group, array_merge( $salt, array( 'stale' ) ) ) ); }

tests.prompt: A long job must never run twice at once. Implement a function that tries to claim a run lock for a supplied job key, storing the lock in the object cache under that key in the 'wpbp_locks' group with a 30 second lifetime. It must return true only for the call that actually claimed the lock: a second attempt while the lock is held returns false, and once the lock is released the next attempt claims it again.
tests.expected_behavior: The claim must use `wp_cache_add()`, which refuses to overwrite an existing key and returns false, rather than `wp_cache_set()` (always true) or a read-then-write pair. Runtime validation claims a key, re-claims it, claims a second key, deletes the first lock and re-claims it, and checks the lock value is actually stored in the 'wpbp_locks' group.
requirements: Store the lock under the supplied key in the 'wpbp_locks' object cache group with a 30 second expiry
Return true only when this call took the lock, false when another holder already has it
Do not overwrite a lock that is already held

required_patterns.description: Claims the lock with an add operation

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_caching_007' ) ) { return false; } if ( true !== wpbp_caching_007( 'wpbp-nightly-sync' ) ) { return false; } if ( false !== wpbp_caching_007( 'wpbp-nightly-sync' ) ) { return false; } if ( false === wp_cache_get( 'wpbp-nightly-sync', 'wpbp_locks' ) ) { return false; } if ( false !== wp_cache_get( 'wpbp-nightly-sync', 'default' ) ) { return false; } if ( true !== wpbp_caching_007( 'wpbp-weekly-report' ) ) { return false; } if ( false !== wpbp_caching_007( 'wpbp-weekly-report' ) ) { return false; } wp_cache_delete( 'wpbp-nightly-sync', 'wpbp_locks' ); if ( true !== wpbp_caching_007( 'wpbp-nightly-sync' ) ) { return false; } return false !== wp_cache_get( 'wpbp-weekly-report', 'wpbp_locks' );
assertions.description: Only the first claim of each key succeeds, and a released lock can be claimed again

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_caching_007( string $job_key ): bool { return (bool) wp_cache_add( $job_key, time(), 'wpbp_locks', 30 ); }
exploit_solutions: function wpbp_caching_007( string $job_key ): bool { wp_cache_set( $job_key, time(), 'wpbp_locks', 30 ); return true; }
function wpbp_caching_007( string $job_key ): bool { return (bool) wp_cache_add( $job_key, time(), 'default', 30 ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that invalidates one named object cache group and nothing else: every key in that group is dropped, while keys in other groups — including the cache WordPress uses for options — survive. Return whether the object cache performed the group invalidation.
tests.expected_behavior: The function uses `wp_cache_flush_group()` (guarded by `wp_cache_supports( 'flush_group' )` if desired) rather than `wp_cache_flush()`, which would empty every group. Runtime validation seeds two custom groups plus a probe in the `options` group, flushes one group, checks only that group is gone, then flushes the second group and checks the options probe is still cached.
requirements: Drop every key in the supplied cache group
Leave keys in every other cache group untouched
Return true when the object cache performed the group invalidation

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_caching_008' ) ) { return false; } if ( true !== wpbp_caching_008( 'wpbp_reports' ) ) { return false; } if ( false !== wp_cache_get( 'wpbp_report_a', 'wpbp_reports' ) || false !== wp_cache_get( 'wpbp_report_b', 'wpbp_reports' ) ) { return false; } if ( 'charlie' !== wp_cache_get( 'wpbp_invoice_a', 'wpbp_invoices' ) ) { return false; } if ( 'delta' !== wp_cache_get( 'wpbp_options_probe', 'options' ) ) { return false; } if ( true !== wpbp_caching_008( 'wpbp_invoices' ) ) { return false; } if ( false !== wp_cache_get( 'wpbp_invoice_a', 'wpbp_invoices' ) ) { return false; } return 'delta' === wp_cache_get( 'wpbp_options_probe', 'options' );
assertions.description: Each named group is emptied while other groups keep their values

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_caching_008( string $group ): bool { if ( ! wp_cache_supports( 'flush_group' ) ) { return false; } return (bool) wp_cache_flush_group( $group ); }
exploit_solutions: function wpbp_caching_008( string $group ): bool { return (bool) wp_cache_flush(); }
function wpbp_caching_008( string $group ): bool { wp_cache_delete( 'wpbp_report_a', $group ); wp_cache_delete( 'wpbp_report_b', $group ); return true; }

tests.prompt: Implement a hit counter backed by the object cache: given a counter key, increase the count for that key in the 'wpbp_counters' group and return the new total. The first call for a key must return 1 and leave the count stored, later calls return 2, 3 and so on, and each key counts independently.
tests.expected_behavior: The object cache cannot increment a key that does not exist yet — `wp_cache_incr()` returns false for a missing key — so the implementation has to seed the counter (for example with `wp_cache_add()`/`wp_cache_set()`) before or after a failed increment. Runtime validation counts one key three times, counts a second key once, reads the stored value back from the group, then deletes the key and checks the count restarts at 1.
requirements: Store the count in the object cache under the supplied key in the 'wpbp_counters' group
Return the new total as an integer, starting from 1 for a key that has no stored count
Keep separate keys counting independently

required_patterns.description: Seeds the counter when it does not exist yet

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_caching_009' ) ) { return false; } if ( 1 !== wpbp_caching_009( 'wpbp-views-home' ) ) { return false; } if ( 1 !== (int) wp_cache_get( 'wpbp-views-home', 'wpbp_counters' ) ) { return false; } if ( 2 !== wpbp_caching_009( 'wpbp-views-home' ) ) { return false; } if ( 3 !== wpbp_caching_009( 'wpbp-views-home' ) ) { return false; } if ( 1 !== wpbp_caching_009( 'wpbp-views-about' ) ) { return false; } if ( 3 !== (int) wp_cache_get( 'wpbp-views-home', 'wpbp_counters' ) ) { return false; } if ( 4 !== wpbp_caching_009( 'wpbp-views-home' ) ) { return false; } wp_cache_delete( 'wpbp-views-home', 'wpbp_counters' ); return 1 === wpbp_caching_009( 'wpbp-views-home' ) && 2 === wpbp_caching_009( 'wpbp-views-about' );
assertions.description: Counting starts at 1 per key, keeps rising, is stored in the group, and restarts after the key is dropped

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_caching_009( string $counter_key ): int { $total = wp_cache_incr( $counter_key, 1, 'wpbp_counters' ); if ( false === $total ) { wp_cache_add( $counter_key, 1, 'wpbp_counters' ); $total = (int) wp_cache_get( $counter_key, 'wpbp_counters' ); } return (int) $total; }
exploit_solutions: function wpbp_caching_009( string $counter_key ): int { return (int) wp_cache_incr( $counter_key, 1, 'wpbp_counters' ); }
function wpbp_caching_009( string $counter_key ): int { $total = (int) wp_cache_get( $counter_key, 'wpbp_counters' ) + 1; wp_cache_set( $counter_key, $total, 'default' ); return $total; }

tests.prompt: Expensive dashboard reports should be computed at most once an hour. Implement a function that returns the report for a supplied report key. When no cached copy exists it calls the supplied compute callback, keeps the result in a transient named 'wpbp_report_' followed by the report key for one hour, and returns it. While the cached copy exists it returns that copy without calling the callback again. Some reports are legitimately empty, and an empty report is still a result worth caching.
tests.expected_behavior: Classic cache-aside over the Transients API: `get_transient()` first, and only a `false` return counts as a miss, so an empty array is served from the cache instead of being recomputed on every request (the common `if ( ! $cached )` bug). The miss path stores the callback's result with `set_transient()` and a one hour expiration. Runtime validation counts callback invocations across repeated calls for two keys, checks the stored transient and its timeout option, caches an empty report, and confirms deleting the transient forces exactly one recompute.
requirements: Call the compute callback with no arguments; it returns the report as an array
Store the report in the transient 'wpbp_report_<report key>' with a one hour expiration
Do not call the callback while a cached report exists, including when the cached report is an empty array

required_patterns.description: Reads the cached report from a transient
Stores the computed report in a transient
Uses the requested transient name prefix

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_caching_010' ) ) { return false; } $calls = 0; $sales = function () use ( &$calls ) { $calls++; return array( 'total' => 40 + $calls, 'currency' => 'EUR' ); }; $first = wpbp_caching_010( 'sales', $sales ); if ( array( 'total' => 41, 'currency' => 'EUR' ) !== $first || 1 !== $calls ) { return false; } if ( $first !== wpbp_caching_010( 'sales', $sales ) || $first !== wpbp_caching_010( 'sales', $sales ) || 1 !== $calls ) { return false; } if ( $first !== get_transient( 'wpbp_report_sales' ) ) { return false; } delete_transient( 'wpbp_report_sales' ); if ( array( 'total' => 42, 'currency' => 'EUR' ) !== wpbp_caching_010( 'sales', $sales ) || 2 !== $calls ) { return false; } return array( 'total' => 42, 'currency' => 'EUR' ) === wpbp_caching_010( 'sales', $sales ) && 2 === $calls;
assertions.description: A cached report is served without calling the callback, and deleting the transient forces one recompute

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_caching_010' ) ) { return false; } $timeout = (int) get_option( '_transient_timeout_wpbp_report_sales' ); $now = time(); return $timeout >= $now + HOUR_IN_SECONDS - 60 && $timeout <= $now + HOUR_IN_SECONDS + 5;
assertions.description: The report transient expires one hour after it was stored

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_caching_010' ) ) { return false; } $calls = 0; $refunds = function () use ( &$calls ) { $calls++; return array(); }; if ( array() !== wpbp_caching_010( 'refunds', $refunds ) || 1 !== $calls ) { return false; } if ( array() !== get_transient( 'wpbp_report_refunds' ) ) { return false; } if ( array() !== wpbp_caching_010( 'refunds', $refunds ) || array() !== wpbp_caching_010( 'refunds', $refunds ) ) { return false; } return 1 === $calls;
assertions.description: An empty report is cached and served without recomputing it

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_caching_010( string $report_key, callable $compute ): array { $name = 'wpbp_report_' . $report_key; $cached = get_transient( $name ); if ( false !== $cached ) { return (array) $cached; } $report = (array) call_user_func( $compute ); set_transient( $name, $report, HOUR_IN_SECONDS ); return $report; }
exploit_solutions: function wpbp_caching_010( string $report_key, callable $compute ): array { $cached = get_transient( 'wpbp_report_' . $report_key ); if ( $cached ) { return $cached; } $report = call_user_func( $compute ); set_transient( 'wpbp_report_' . $report_key, $report, HOUR_IN_SECONDS ); return $report; }

function wpbp_caching_010( string $report_key, callable $compute ): array { $cached = get_transient( 'wpbp_report_' . $report_key ); if ( false !== $cached ) { return $cached; } $report = call_user_func( $compute ); set_transient( 'wpbp_report_' . $report_key, $report ); return $report; }

function wpbp_caching_010( string $report_key, callable $compute ): array { $found = false; $cached = wp_cache_get( 'wpbp_report_' . $report_key, 'wpbp_reports', false, $found ); if ( $found ) { return $cached; } $report = call_user_func( $compute ); wp_cache_set( 'wpbp_report_' . $report_key, $report, 'wpbp_reports', HOUR_IN_SECONDS ); return $report; }

tests.prompt: Every page on this site lists the published 'wpbp_event' posts, so the list of their IDs is cached in a transient named 'wpbp_event_ids'. Implement a function that returns the IDs of all published 'wpbp_event' posts, served from that transient when it holds a list and rebuilt from the database (and cached again) when it does not. Visitors must never see a stale list: whenever a 'wpbp_event' post is created, updated, trashed or deleted, drop the cached list. Saving posts of any other type must leave the cached list in place.
tests.expected_behavior: The gateway reads `get_transient( 'wpbp_event_ids' )` and rebuilds with an IDs-only query on a miss. Invalidation is registered by the submission itself on hooks that cover create, update, trash and permanent delete (for example `clean_post_cache`, or `save_post_wpbp_event` plus `deleted_post`), filtered to the 'wpbp_event' post type. Runtime validation proves the list really comes from the transient by inserting an event row directly with `$wpdb` (no hooks fire, no core cache is bumped) and expecting it to stay hidden, saves an unrelated post and expects the list to stay cached, then creates, unpublishes, trashes and force-deletes events through the post APIs and expects a fresh list each time.
requirements: Return the IDs of published 'wpbp_event' posts as integers, in any order
Cache the list in the 'wpbp_event_ids' transient and serve it from there while it exists
Drop the cached list when a 'wpbp_event' post is created, updated, trashed or deleted, and only then

required_patterns.description: Drops the cached list on changes

runtime_checks.setup: register_post_type( 'wpbp_event', array( 'public' => true, 'label' => 'WPBP Events' ) ); delete_transient( 'wpbp_event_ids' ); $events = array(); foreach ( array( 'Launch', 'Meetup', 'Workshop' ) as $title ) { $events[] = (int) wp_insert_post( array( 'post_type' => 'wpbp_event', 'post_title' => 'WPBP ' . $title, 'post_status' => 'publish' ) ); } $draft = (int) wp_insert_post( array( 'post_type' => 'wpbp_event', 'post_title' => 'WPBP Draft Event', 'post_status' => 'draft' ) ); $GLOBALS['wpbp_caching_011'] = array( 'events' => $events, 'cleanup' => array_merge( $events, array( $draft ) ) );

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_caching_011' ) ) { return false; } global $wpdb; $f = $GLOBALS['wpbp_caching_011'] ?? array(); if ( empty( $f['events'] ) || in_array( 0, $f['events'], true ) ) { return false; } $list = function () { $ids = array_map( 'intval', (array) wpbp_caching_011() ); sort( $ids ); return $ids; }; $expected = $f['events']; sort( $expected ); if ( $expected !== $list() ) { return false; } if ( false === get_transient( 'wpbp_event_ids' ) ) { return false; } $now = current_time( 'mysql' ); $now_gmt = current_time( 'mysql', true ); $wpdb->insert( $wpdb->posts, array( 'post_author' => 1, 'post_date' => $now, 'post_date_gmt' => $now_gmt, 'post_content' => '', 'post_title' => 'WPBP Imported Event', 'post_excerpt' => '', 'post_status' => 'publish', 'post_type' => 'wpbp_event', 'post_name' => 'wpbp-imported-event', 'to_ping' => '', 'pinged' => '', 'post_modified' => $now, 'post_modified_gmt' => $now_gmt, 'post_content_filtered' => '', 'guid' => '' ) ); $imported = (int) $wpdb->insert_id; $GLOBALS['wpbp_caching_011']['cleanup'][] = $imported; if ( ! $imported || $expected !== $list() ) { return false; } $other = (int) wp_insert_post( array( 'post_title' => 'WPBP Unrelated Post', 'post_status' => 'publish' ) ); $GLOBALS['wpbp_caching_011']['cleanup'][] = $other; $page = (int) wp_insert_post( array( 'post_type' => 'page', 'post_title' => 'WPBP Unrelated Page', 'post_status' => 'publish' ) ); $GLOBALS['wpbp_caching_011']['cleanup'][] = $page; return $other && $page && $expected === $list();
assertions.description: The list is served from the transient, and saving other post types keeps it cached

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_caching_011' ) ) { return false; } global $wpdb; $f = $GLOBALS['wpbp_caching_011'] ?? array(); if ( empty( $f['events'] ) ) { return false; } $list = function () { $ids = array_map( 'intval', (array) wpbp_caching_011() ); sort( $ids ); return $ids; }; $published = function () use ( $wpdb ) { $ids = array_map( 'intval', $wpdb->get_col( "SELECT ID FROM {$wpdb->posts} WHERE post_type = 'wpbp_event' AND post_status = 'publish'" ) ); sort( $ids ); return $ids; }; $list(); $new = (int) wp_insert_post( array( 'post_type' => 'wpbp_event', 'post_title' => 'WPBP Hackathon', 'post_status' => 'publish' ) ); $GLOBALS['wpbp_caching_011']['cleanup'][] = $new; $after_create = $list(); if ( ! $new || ! in_array( $new, $after_create, true ) || $published() !== $after_create ) { return false; } wp_update_post( array( 'ID' => $f['events'][0], 'post_status' => 'draft' ) ); $after_update = $list(); if ( in_array( $f['events'][0], $after_update, true ) || $published() !== $after_update ) { return false; } wp_trash_post( $f['events'][1] ); $after_trash = $list(); if ( in_array( $f['events'][1], $after_trash, true ) || $published() !== $after_trash ) { return false; } wp_delete_post( $f['events'][2], true ); $after_delete = $list(); return ! in_array( $f['events'][2], $after_delete, true ) && $published() === $after_delete;

tests.prompt: Report the shop's total stock: the sum of the numeric 'wpbp_stock' custom field over every published 'wpbp_product' post. Summing it is a database aggregate that is too slow to run on every request, so keep the computed total in the object cache group 'wpbp_stats'. Do not register your own post or meta hooks to invalidate it. Instead, tie the cached total to the change marker WordPress itself maintains for posts, so that whenever WordPress records a change to posts or post meta the old total is never served again.
tests.expected_behavior: The cache key (or salt) includes `wp_cache_get_last_changed( 'posts' )`, the marker core bumps from `clean_post_cache()` and from the `added/updated/deleted_post_meta` actions, so invalidation is implicit. Either `wp_cache_get()`/`wp_cache_set()` with the marker in the key or `wp_cache_get_salted()`/`wp_cache_set_salted()` (6.9+) passes. The aggregate runs once per marker value. Runtime validation checks the total, confirms a value is stored in the 'wpbp_stats' group, edits a stock value directly in the database (and drops that post's meta cache) without bumping the marker to prove the total is served from cache, then bumps the marker explicitly, updates meta through the API, and publishes a draft product, expecting a fresh total after each.
requirements: Return the total as an integer; only published 'wpbp_product' posts count
Store the computed total in the 'wpbp_stats' object cache group
Serve the cached total until WordPress marks posts as changed, without registering invalidation hooks

forbidden_patterns.description: Invalidates through its own post or meta hooks instead of the last-changed marker

tests.prompt: Profile badges are expensive to compute and are cached in the object cache group 'wpbp_badges', keyed by user ID. Implement a function that takes a list of user IDs and a compute callback and returns a map of user ID to badge. On sites with a persistent object cache every cache call is a network round trip, so a whole lookup may read the cache only once and write it only once: fetch every requested badge in a single cache read, call the callback only for the users whose badge was not cached, and save all of the newly computed badges in a single cache write.
tests.expected_behavior: The function uses `wp_cache_get_multiple()` for the read and `wp_cache_set_multiple()` (or `wp_cache_add_multiple()`) for the write, never a per-key `wp_cache_get()`/`wp_cache_set()` loop. Misses are the keys whose value comes back `false`. Runtime validation swaps in a `WP_Object_Cache` subclass that counts top-level calls for the 'wpbp_badges' group, seeds two badges, and requires one batch read, zero single reads, the callback for exactly the two misses, one batch write and zero single writes; a second lookup over already cached users must not call the callback or write per key.
requirements: Call the compute callback with a single user ID; it returns that user's badge string
Return every requested user ID mapped to its badge, cached or newly computed
Use one object cache read for all requested IDs and at most one write for the newly computed badges

required_patterns.description: Reads every badge in one batch
Writes the computed badges in one batch
